title: Mechanistic insights into the gastroprotective and anti-Helicobacter pylori effects of novel Smyrnium olusatrum extracts through NF-kappaB, IBA1, and COX-2 modulation.
authors: Terbeche, Manel; Deramchia, Nawel; Amari, Nesrine Ouda; Pachura-Hanusek, Natalia; Szumny, Antoni; Ouadah, Karim; Zawilak-Pawlik, Anna; Muraszko, Jakub; Moos, Torben
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物提取物的胃保护与抗幽门螺杆菌作用，仅涉及NF-kB/COX-2的小分子对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: ETHNOBOTANICAL RELEVANCE: Smyrnium olusatrum L. (Apiaceae), commonly known as Alexanders, has been traditionally used in Mediterranean ethnomedicine to alleviate digestive disorders, gastric discomfort, and inflammatory conditions. However, its gastroprotective and anti-Helicobacter pylori properties have not yet been scientifically investigated. Given that oxidative stress and inflammation play pivotal roles in peptic ulcer pathogenesis and aggravate H. pylori-induced mucosal damage, investigating traditionally used gastrointestinal remedies such as S. olusatrum is particularly relevant. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study evaluated the gastroprotective and anti-H. pylori activities of S. olusatrum extracts and investigated their underlying anti-inflammatory mechanisms. METHODS: Gastroprotection was assessed in rats through ulcer index determination, gastric secretion analysis, and histological examination. To elucidate the mechanisms underlying the observed gastroprotective effects, immunofluorescence targeting nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kappaB) and ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1 (IBA1) was performed. Major phytoconstituents identified by LC-MS/MS were further subjected to molecular docking against NF-kappaB and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2). Additionally, an in vitro anti-H. pylori activity was assessed. RESULTS: Both extracts exhibited significant dose-dependent gastroprotection (p < 0.001), with the highest doses reducing ulcer indices to 5.96% +/- 5.37 (root extract) and 0.70% +/- 0.39 (seed extract), preserving mucosal architecture, minimizing edema, and decreasing neutrophil infiltration. NF-kappaB nuclear translocation and IBA1-positive macrophage recruitment were significantly suppressed (p < 0.001). Docking analysis suggested favorable binding affinities of myricetin and luteolin toward NF-kappaB and COX-2. The seed extract showed selective anti-H. pylori activity, whereas the root extract was inactive. CONCLUSION: These findings provide experimental support for the traditional gastrointestinal use of S. olusatrum, highlighting its potential as a promising ethnopharmacological candidate for ulcer management.
abstract_zh: 民族植物学相关性：Smyrnium olusatrum L.（伞形科），俗称亚历山大草，在地中海民族医学中传统上用于缓解消化系统疾病、胃部不适和炎症性疾病。然而，其胃保护和抗幽门螺杆菌（Helicobacter pylori）特性尚未得到科学研究。鉴于氧化应激和炎症在消化性溃疡发病机制中发挥关键作用，并加重H. pylori诱导的黏膜损伤，研究S. olusatrum等传统使用的胃肠道药物具有特别意义。研究目的：本研究评估了S. olusatrum提取物的胃保护和抗H. pylori活性，并探讨了其潜在的抗炎机制。方法：通过溃疡指数测定、胃分泌分析和组织学检查在大鼠中评估胃保护作用。为阐明观察到的胃保护效应背后的机制，进行了针对核因子κB（NF-kappaB）和离子化钙结合适配分子1（IBA1）的免疫荧光检测。通过LC-MS/MS鉴定的主要植物成分进一步与NF-kappaB和环氧合酶-2（COX-2）进行分子对接。此外，评估了体外抗H. pylori活性。结果：两种提取物均表现出显著的剂量依赖性胃保护作用（p < 0.001），最高剂量将溃疡指数分别降至5.96% +/- 5.37（根提取物）和0.70% +/- 0.39（种子提取物），保护黏膜结构，减少水肿，并降低中性粒细胞浸润。NF-kappaB核转位和IBA1阳性巨噬细胞募集被显著抑制（p < 0.001）。对接分析提示杨梅素和木犀草素对NF-kappaB和COX-2具有有利的结合亲和力。种子提取物表现出选择性抗H. pylori活性，而根提取物无活性。结论：这些发现为S. olusatrum的传统胃肠道用途提供了实验支持，突显其作为溃疡管理中有前景的民族药理学候选物的潜力。
